import os
import time
import pytest
from pathlib import Path

# Import the public API that is available in the codebase
from doorstop.core.document import Document
from doorstop.core.item import Item
from doorstop.core.types import UID, Level
from doorstop.core.base import BaseFileObject


@pytest.fixture
def temp_dir(tmp_path):
    """Return a temporary directory for test artifacts."""
    return tmp_path


def _create_document(path: Path, name: str = "test_doc") -> Document:
    """Helper to create a new document in the given path."""
    doc = Document.new(path, name=name)
    doc.save()
    return doc


def _add_items(doc: Document, count: int) -> list[Item]:
    """Add `count` items to the document and return the list."""
    items = []
    for i in range(1, count + 1):
        uid = UID(f"{i:03d}")
        item = Item.new(doc, uid=uid, level=Level.load_level(i))
        item.text = f"Requirement {i}"
        item.save()
        items.append(item)
    return items


def test_U02_4__Finite_State__TC_001(temp_dir):
    """
    Verify initial state and secure storage
    Expected: Requirements stored securely and permanently
    """
    # Create a document
    doc_path = temp_dir / "doc"
    doc = _create_document(doc_path)

    # The document file should exist and be non-empty
    assert doc.path.exists(), "Document file does not exist"
    assert doc.path.stat().st_size > 0, "Document file is empty"

    # The document should be readable and contain YAML header
    with open(doc.path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        content = f.read()
    assert "---" in content, "Document does not contain YAML header"

    # Ensure the file is not writable by others (basic permission check)
    mode = os.stat(doc.path).st_mode
    assert not (mode & 0o022), "Document file is world-writable"

def test_U02_4__Finite_State__TC_007(temp_dir):
    """
    Verify system behavior at boundary conditions
    Expected: System maintains secure storage and efficient change management at boundary conditions
    """
    # Create a document with minimal requirements
    doc_path = temp_dir / "boundary_doc"
    doc = _create_document(doc_path)

    # Add a single item
    items = _add_items(doc, 1)
    assert len(items) == 1, "Boundary doc should have exactly one item"

    # Verify secure storage of the single item
    assert doc.path.exists(), "Document file missing"
    assert doc.path.stat().st_size > 0, "Document file empty"

    # Simulate a large number of changes by adding many items quickly
    start = time.time()
    _add_items(doc, 500)
    duration = time.time() - start

    # Ensure the system handled the changes efficiently
    assert duration < 3, f"Handling 500 changes took too long: {duration:.2f}s"

    # Final check: document still exists and is readable
    assert doc.path.exists(), "Document file missing after changes"
    with open(doc.path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        content = f.read()
    assert "---" in content, "Document YAML header missing after changes"
